argv: Completed without hints or rejected gestures. Measuring cargo for a broad ferry and measuring a passage for a slim skiff was the best contrast: same wood and tools, different purpose and arrangement. Build steps were legible, but the second assembly chain felt routine, with little choice or surprise. Launch feedback was only Placed; miller payoff arrived on advance, while rescue ended with Journey complete and still-present waiting-fisher text. I continued to see the second job and ending, not because recipes were uncertain. Beyond recipes, the story conveyed that material, skilled making, shape, and intended use explain different aspects of the boat, and a sound boat is not suitable for every task. Much of that was explicitly told in descriptions rather than discovered through consequences. Logical-interface impressions only, not human-fun evidence. No desire to replay the same path.
